item.title: Sven Ulreich not sure if he will retire after this season
item.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - MAY 6: Goalkeeper Manuel Neuer of FC Bayern München (R) and Goalkeeper Sven Ulreich of FC Bayern München look on ahead of the UEFA Champions League 2025/26 Semi Final Second Leg match between FC Bayern München and Paris Saint-Germain at Football Arena Munich on May 6, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Sebastian El-Saqqa - firo sportphoto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich is currently operating under the impression that Manuel Neuer is going to retire after the end of this season, though they maintain that he is still the club’s number one keeper for the time being. He is currently out injured due to a partial tendon tear in his right foot sustained in Bayern’s win at Mainz earlier this month. While neither Neuer nor the club has said anything outright about what will happen after this season when his contract expires, the club has been preparing for life without him. The veteran keeper has been mentoring Jonas Urbig ever since the young keeper joined from FC Köln in the winter of 2025 for a fee of around €10 million. With Neuer’s injury history since Urbig arrived in Munich, the 23-year-old has gotten a considerable number of matches for the German Rekordmeister and has shown that he is ready to become the club’s number one keeper once Neuer is no longer in the pictu re. Both Julian Nagelsmann and Jürgen Klopp have even selected him for the senior Germany squad for recent international breaks, after he earned his first call-up in March of this year under Nagelsmann. For Urbig, the pathway is clear, and while what will happen with Neuer at the end of the season remains to be seen, retirement is looking like the most likely outcome. Even so, that still leaves the club with the question of what will happen with fellow veteran keeper Sven Ulreich. His contract is also set to expire this summer, and he hasn’t played a competitive match for Bayern since th e 1–1 draw with Bayer Leverkusen in the Bundesliga back in March. Prior to that game, he had gone over 500 days without a competitive appearance, largely because he had to take a substantial amount of time off for personal reasons. When asked whether he would be retiring with Neuer at the end of the season, Ulreich left the door open to all options. “I’m 38, Manuel is 40, so that’s a legitimate question. I will speak to FC Bayern in the near future about how things will proceed and what the club wants. I can’t speak on Manu’s behalf about what happens afte r the season, but I’m making everything dependent on him right now,” the veteran keeper explained (via @iMia SanMia ). When asked whether it was still conceivable that he would continue playing even if Neuer retires, Ulreich replied, “Anything is possible as long as I feel good, healthy, and fit. That’s currently the case. However, I’ve also learned that things can change quickly. I live in the here and now, and at the moment, I enjoy going out onto the pitch every day.” Bayern needs to hone in on what its plan will be.

item.title: Trading for Teoscar Hernandez is best for 2026 and beyond
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 12: Teoscar Hernández #37 of the Los Angeles Dodgers hits a sacrifice fly in the first inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game two of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 12, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Phillies’ quest to solve their long-standing production issues in the outfield was thwarted somewhat when Japanese superstar Teruaki Sato signed a six-year, $120 million deal with the Chicago Cubs earlier this week. It had been hoped that the 27-year-old Triple Crown winner might become the first Japanese import to come directly from Japan to Philadelphia, but it was unsurprisingly not to be. Dave Dombrowski has acknowledged the Phillies need another everyday outfielder on the roster and, with Alec Bohm now a Kansas City Royal after signing a two-year, $20 million contract, they desperately need a productive right-handed bat in the middle of their lineup. Understandably, much of the attention has turned to 32-year-old veteran free agents Seiya Suzuki and Randy Arozarena. I’ve gone over the pros and cons of these two players in a previous post , and recent reports indicate Suzuki would prefer to play on the west coast, all things being equal. Seiya Suzuki is down to four teams, according to Sanspo Japan: Padres Blue Jays Phillies Mariners A source in the American baseball world revealed, "If the salary and contract terms were the same for multiple interested teams, he would choose the Padres." Another source said… pic.twitter.com/pCuI8QQug1 — Phillies Tailgate (@PhilsTailgate) November 27, 2026 I’d prefer Suzuki to Arozarena for the reasons I laid out in my article linked above. He is a more patient and consistent hitter and would bring a legitimate right-handed power to the middle of the Phils’ order. He also plays better defense than Arozarena, and all of the behind-the-numbers metrics indicate Arozarena’s otherworldly offensive performance a season ago may not be repeatable. All things being equal, signing Suzuki makes the most sense for 2027 and ‘28, but there is one other solution that could be wiser than committing at least $20 million a year for half a decade to a player well into their late-30s. The Los Angeles Dodgers are expected to make 34-year-old outfielder Teoscar Hernandez available in a trade this off-season. Whether that happens before or after the presumed lockout that will begin on December 2 is unknown. For a team like the Phillies, pursuing Hernandez in a trade rather than committing to Suzuki or Arozarena makes more sense from a long-term perspective. Two years ago, in his first season after signing a free agent contract with the Dodgers, Hernandez was an All Star. In his age-31 season he posted an OPS of .840, an OPS+ of 135, won a Silver Slugger Award and mashed 33 home runs with 99 RBIs and 84 runs scored. item.title: Colin and Mauleón: the Natalia duo who shook up Chivas Femenil's XI
item.description: Colin and Mauleón: the Natalia duo who shook up Chivas Femenil's XI With a few weeks left in the women’s league’s Apertura 2026, it is worth taking stock of how the season has gone for Chivas Femenil . The team is once again in the Liga Femenil Semifinals, finished second in Group B, and improved on several of its own benchmarks in the division, both in performance and results. Of course, this comes down to a collective effort, with quality in every area of the red-and-white squad, which has also strengthened in recent transfer windows. In the latest window, the club brought in 2 players who are now undisputed starters, have made a major impact on Antonio Contreras ’ system, and share a middle name. Natalia Colin and Natalia Mauleón arrived and broke into Guadalajara’s starting lineup, strengthening a team that already had a solid foundation but has continued to evolve thanks to both players’ contributions. Colin joined from Tigres, while Mauleón arrived from Pachuca with a clear aim: to add quality on the ball. Let’s start with Mauleón, who took part in the Rojiblanca Preseason and made her debut on Matchday 1 against Gallos, making a significant impact on the pitch. She changed the team’s dynamic through her distribution, pressing after losing possession, and chance creation, offering a taste of what she would deliver throughout the tournament. ‘Mau’ played all 16 league matches, averaging 81 minutes per game, providing 5 assists and recording 91% passing accuracy in the opposition half from midfield. For her part, Colin could not take part in the Rojiblanca Preseason because she was called up to the Mexican national team for the Central American and Caribbean Games, where she won gold with El Tri. But her eagerness to wear the colors of the Rebaño Sagrado was even greater: she flew from Santo Domingo to Puebla to make her first appearance for the team just days later. She came on as a substitute at Estadio Cuauhtémoc and has not relinquished her place in Guadalajara’s lineup since. At center back, Natalia has developed an excellent understanding with Cristina Ferral and Samantha López , strengthening the heart of the defense. She has even played as a holding midfielder, thanks to her reading of the game, anticipation, and vision on the ball, which allow her to win back possession and launch attacks for Chivas Femenil . She has made 15 appearances, played 1,298 minutes, and averaged 5 ball recoveries per match, alongside 88% passing accuracy in her own half. item.title: Sheffield Wednesday vs Reading: 2026/27 Match Preview
item.description: Reading haven’t been on the best form in recent times, with back-to-back losses glooming in the fans’ faces. Kyreece Lisbie not being involved has thrown everything out of whack, but the return of a fully fit George Earthy will bring hope into Reading supporters’ eyes. Sheffield Wednesday were one of my favourites to go up this season and they really are proving that. They’re in fourth place currently, Davis Keillor-Dunn and Louie Barry are on form and it’s going to be a good game. Reading fans are screaming for Leam Richardson’s head again just after he’s been linked to take over multiple other jobs. I want to know your opinion! Saturday November 28 brings football to Hillsborough. Kick-off is at 3pm and there’s a capacity of 39,814, so fill that stadium. The referee for this game is Martin Coy, who averages three yellow cards and 22.6 fouls per match. This is the first time we’ve played Wednesday since 2021. This game the Royals won 3-0, with Ballon d’Or top-five finisher Michael Olise, Lucas Joao and Andy Yiadom getting the goals. I miss the team that played that day. What a group of players we had. In this preview I will mention players who have played for both and I will give my predictions. Players who have played for both There are 23 players to play for both Reading and Sheffield Wednesday. Here are four of them: Joe Lumley is currently the starting goalkeeper with the Owls, where he has made 15 appearances so far this season. He has a save percentage of 76.5% and has made 31 saves. For Reading he made 42 appearances with a save percentage of 63%. He made 100 saves that year. Next up is Nathaniel Chalobah. He made 31 appearances for Sheffield Wednesday over the previous two seasons, scoring two and assisting one. He played 20 matches for Reading 10 years prior, scoring one and assisting two. Will Keane played 13 matches for the Owls in 2014. That season he scored three goals and didn’t get an assist. For Reading he played 14 games, scoring two goals and also failing to get an assist for the Royals. Finally we have Jack Marriott . In 2020 he played 13 games for Wednesday, managing neither a goal nor an assist. Comparing that to now, he has so far played 38 games for Reading, scoring 27 goals and getting four assists. He is on fire this season and could be the difference-maker this weekend. My predictions Joel Pereira will start in goal. Udoka Godwin-Malife, Paudie O’Connor, Benn Ward and Haydon Roberts will be the backline. Lewis Wing and Andy Rinomhota will be the defensive two. Leaving Daniel Kyerewaa, George Earthy and Josh Stokes to be the attacking midfielders. Marriott will of course be up top. Score prediction: 1-1 Good luck to those going to the game! Come on you Royals!

item.description: GOODYEAR, AZ: Los Angeles Angels No. 1 prospect Arjun Nimmala in the Salt River Rafters' dugout during an Arizona Fall League game against the Mesa Solar Sox at Goodyear Ballpark on Oct. 17, 2026. (Photo by Brandon Sloter/Getty Images) Getty Images Arjun Nimmala showcased skills in the 2026 Arizona Fall League at age 21 that just might transfer to the Los Angeles Angels’ starting lineup before he turns 22. Pretty good for a kid who concentrated on baseball only after giving up cricket, soccer and basketball. Nimmala wants to be the first everyday player of Indian descent in MLB history. Kumar Rocker of the Texas Rangers became the first pitcher with Indian heritage in 2024. Nobody born in India has played in an MLB game. Nimmala hit .304 and displayed good power at the plate and fine fielding at shortstop this fall for the Mesa Solar Sox – the sixth team he played for in 2026. “The conviction into what he does is really impressive,” Mesa hitting coach Jacob Caples told Jesse Borek of MLB.com. “He’s able to come in every day, know exactly what he needs, know the adjustments that he needs to make, and to be honest with you, I don’t think he thinks anyone’s better than he is. item.title: Brutal News: Patrick Kane Lands On IR, Blackhawks Make Corresponding Move
item.description: The Chicago Blackhawks can’t seem to shed the injury bug. Already without captain Connor Bedard and No. 1 defenseman Bowen Byram , the Blackhawks have now placed winger Patrick Kane on injured reserve with a lower-body ailment retroactive to Nov. 25. Yup. #Blackhawks have placed Patrick Kane on injured reserve with a lower-body injury, retroactive to Nov. 25. Landon Slaggert has been recalled from Rockford. Kane will miss at least the next 3 games. He’s eligible to return next Thursday in Nashville. pic.twitter.com/Hu5BuLhgba — Jack Bushman (@JackBushman2) November 27, 2026 Kane exited Wednesday’s 3-1 win over the Seattle Kraken late in the third period after blocking a shot with his right leg/foot in the defensive zone. The 38-year-old veteran gingerly skated off the ice and went immediately into the locker room. Kane didn’t return for the final 3:01, and he’ll now miss at least the next three games. #Blackhawks officially place Patrick Kane (lower body) on injured reserve retroactive to Nov. 25. He blocked a shot off his right foot/ankle at the end of the game on Wednesday. pic.twitter.com/Dw1nMu87GF — Charlie Roumeliotis (@CRoumeliotis) November 27, 2026 Per NHL guidelines, Kane must remain on injured reserve for a minimum of seven days, meaning he’s eligible to return next Thursday against the Nashville Predators. item.title: Anthony Kim’s Return Is The Best Story In Modern Golf
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Anthony Kim is back, and he is not here to play small ball. The man who vanished for twelve and a half years just dropped the most honest interview in golf history. He spoke to Joe Rogan about his darkest days, his battle with addiction, and the family that pulled him out of the hole. GolfMagic reported that Kim opened up about a life he once struggled to imagine living. The numbers from his first tournament back look ugly to most fans. He finished 33 strokes behind the leader. That would have ended a normal career. Kim saw it differently. He told Rogan he was “so excited after that tournament” because he felt he could win the next week. His wife Emily believed him even when the rest of the world did not. He used the hate from online comments as fuel to practice longer. “When I say I’m done, I think about those comments and I stay out there for 30 minutes longer,” he said. The Turnaround Is Real That grit paid off in February 2026. Kim won LIV Golf Adelaide with a final-round nine-under-par 63. At the start of the day, he was five shots behind Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau. He earned his first win in nearly 16 years by passing two of the sport’s most prominent figures. The crowd on the 18th green embraced the underdog story. Kim celebrated a three-shot victory that meant far more than a trophy. A New Kind of Player The old Anthony Kim was a fearless star who won three times before age 26. He was part of the winning 2008 Ryder Cup team. The new Anthony Kim is a 41-year-old father who prays for another day. He told Rogan that as a kid he prayed he would not wake up. “Now, when I wake up, I pray to God that I get one more day just so I could see that beautiful smile of my daughter and my wife who saved my life,” Kim said. His return to the winner’s circle is a rare feat in the modern game.

item.description: Odegaard Napoli Arsenal Martin Odegaard has insisted he is not worried about his Arsenal contract and hopes to stay at the club for many more years. The captain's current deal runs until 2028, but he is confident new terms will be agreed as the Premier League champions continue to tie down their key players, with Mikel Arteta's side preparing to host Manchester City on Sunday. Odegaard relaxed over contract future Arsenal are tying down the likes of Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, David Raya and Piero Hincapie to new long-term contracts, and Odegaard has told Sky Sports News he expects to follow suit, with his current deal set to expire in 2028. "It's not something I stress about," Odegaard said. "I've said it so many times, I'm so happy here, I love it here. Hopefully I can stay for many more years - and I think the club is happy as well. So it's no stress, we'll sort it out." Captain wants to 'win everything' Odegaard, who has been linked with Bayern Munich, said while on international duty with Norway earlier this month that he hoped to stay at Arsenal "for a long time", but admitted talks over a new deal had not started yet. "The main thing is to focus on the pitch, and then we'll see what happens," he added. "I want to win more things here for sure. I want to win everything with Arsenal. The Premier League again, the Champions League, the cups - that's what we want. We want to win everything." 'We have everything here' The 27-year-old insisted the team comes first. item.title: Decline of deities - the long game the All Blacks cannot afford to lose
item.description: Codie Taylor led the New Zealand haka against England before the 37-12 defeat last Saturday [Getty Images] For decades, the All Blacks have defied gravity. Despite a population, player pool and bank balance smaller than most of their rivals, New Zealand's rugby team have become sporting shorthand for success. Deservedly so. No other team comes close to them. England beat the All Blacks this year and last. They play them again on Saturday aiming for a hat-trick. But, England would need that winning streak to continue until around 2050 just to level up a lop-sided historical head-to-head. New Zealand have won 36 times to England's 10 in their 121-year rivalry. For every other nation in Test rugby, the story is the same. New Zealand have the superior record against them all. A section on the All Blacks' website, titled Rivalries, opens by listing South Africa's 40% winning record in their meetings. And the numbers only drop from there. But New Zealand's grip on the global game appears looser now than ever. If they lose to England on Saturday, it may not much sway the historical balance between the two teams. But it would be a sixth defeat in a calendar year, a total matched only once before in the All Blacks past, back in 1949 when a split squad played two Test series in Australia and apartheid South Africa at the same time. New Zealand's win percentage in 2026 is 58.3%, their third lowest for any year since the start of professionalism. This campaign, marked by an exhausting schedule and four Tests away to the world champion Springboks, is in keeping with a recent trend. Since the end of the 2010s - a period in which an all-time great team captured back-to-back world titles - New Zealand have come off the boil. The 2020s are on course to be their least successful decade since the 1970s. This current crop of All Blacks are suffering not just by comparison to the previous generation, but when set against every other modern predecessor. One reason may be a source of strength turning against them. The All Blacks' culture of promoting within and establishing coaching dynasties was seen as key when they were winning. A thread ran through the Graham Henry, Steve Hansen and Ian Foster succession in the 2010s glory days. The latter two served under their predecessor and the first two earned their Test stripes with Wales, before taking the top job. All were schooled as coaches in New Zealand and steeped in the country's rugby traditions. The in-house production line of leaders ensured continuity and protected a team ethos that has been admired and written about everywhere. But, in a modern world in which opposition tactics are quickly picked apart and best practice spreads fast, has adherence to tradition held back the team? item.title: 3 reasons why Alabama will defeat Auburn in Iron Bowl, 3 why not
item.description: Every time Alabama and Auburn get together it is a big game, and once again, this year's Iron Bowl also has a lot at stake. Alabama (9-2 overall, 6-2 SEC) is looking to lock up their spot in the College Football Playoff (CFP), while Auburn (7-4, 4-4) is looking to keep up their momentum under first-year head coach Alex Golesh and to wrap up the regular season in the top 25. For Alabama, a win would fully lock them into the CFP, as well as potentially the SEC championship game depending on what happens elsewhere, while a loss would mean some sweating over the next week with them on the bubble heading into Selection Sunday. Auburn meanwhile has won three-straight and has some momentum going as they are looking to surge into the top 25 with a late-season run in the first season of a new era. What could decide the winner of this Iron Bowl? Well, here are three reasons why Alabama will win, as well as three reasons they might not. Why: Alabama's pass rush against Auburn's offensive line One of the biggest areas of weakness this season for Auburn has been allowing sacks. Auburn is bottom five nationally and tied for worst in the SEC having allowed 39 sacks this season. That's just over 3.5 per game. On the flip-side, Alabama's defense ranks in the top 25 nationally in producing sacks this year with 31. Now, not all of Auburn's sacks allowed is on the offensive line. There have been issues this season with Byrum Brown holding the ball too long. But, whichever the case, this is an opportunity for Alabama's pass rush to have a big day, although they will have to stay disciplined. Why Not: Auburn's pass rush against Alabama's offensive line There's a similar story, not as extreme though, on the flip-side. Alabama's offensive line ranks just outside the top 100 nationally in sacks allowed with 28. Auburn's pass rush has been slightly better than Alabama's at getting to the quarterback this season with 33 sacks, tied for tenth-most nationally. If Auburn is going to slow down Alabama's passing attack, one way to do it will to be to get after the quarterback. Why: Success to be had against Auburn's defense Auburn's defense has disappointed at times this season. It was a hyped-up unit in the offseason after retaining DJ Durkin as defensive coordinator, but the Tigers defense has struggled at times this season. Auburn's defense is middle of the pack in the SEC in scoring defense, allowing 23.9 points per game. However, it is bottom three in the SEC in yards allowed, passing yards allowed, and rushing yards allowed per game. Auburn is also outside the top 60 nationally in third down defense, and in their losses is when those issues have really shown up. In Auburn's four losses they are allowing 37.8 points per game. In their four SEC wins, Auburn is allowing 17.8 points per game. While it's obvious to say "they generally lose when they allow more points," that is a pathway for Alabama to win the game with their very talented offense led by a superstar quarterback

item.title: Mercedes set pace in eventful Qatar second practice
item.description: Gasly hit an advertising board after leaving the track [Getty Images] World champion Kimi Antonelli set the pace ahead of Mercedes team-mate George Russell in a disrupted second practice at the Qatar Grand Prix. Italian Antonelli was 0.127 seconds quicker than Russell on the medium tyre, as neither driver set a time on the soft compound because of two red flags that punctuated the session. Lewis Hamilton also came to halt after his Ferrari lost power, with a virtual safety car deployed so the marshals could come to the seven-time world champion's aid. The McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri plus Red Bull's Max Verstappen completed the top five at the Lusail International Circuit, with the trio setting soft-tyre times that were more than four tenths adrift of the two Mercedes. The first red flag was to clear gravel off the track after an incident for Ferrari's Charles Leclerc early on, while the other was to recover the Alpine of Pierre Gasly following a high-speed spin. Frenchman Gasly hit a marker board before beaching himself after taking too much kerb at Turn 14 in the middle of the qualifying simulation runs. The interruptions led to the second hour being extended by 13 minutes to allow drivers more time on track in the representative conditions. "It was a productive day," said Antonelli. "We tried a lot of things on the car between FP1 and FP2, but in FP2, it seemed like we did a step back with the car. "But it was very interesting to see how the car behaved after those changes. It's not easy." Antonelli, who secured his maiden title in Mexico City earlier this month, was also fastest in the opening session on the mediums. Mercedes did fit the 20-year-old with the soft tyre in the first hour, but he failed to set a lap time on them. He said he feels it will be close between himself and Russell for the race victory, but added: "You can never write off Max [Verstappen] and the others." Norris, meanwhile, said Mercedes "were in a different category" to McLaren, highlighting the Silver Arrows "were quicker in every single corner by miles". The 2025 world champion added: "We seem in a relatively decent position, similar on pace with Red Bull, and similar-ish to Ferrari. So I'd say it's OK." Four-time title winner Verstappen said it had been a "difficult day" following his issues with heavy steering towards the end of the session. "The balance of the car is probably too disconnected at the moment to go fast," he added. "It's costing us quite a bit of lap time." Hamilton also had a moment with Verstappen that was noted by the race control. The Briton was on a flying lap when he got too close to the Dutchman, who was on a long run. Verstappen said Hamilton had moved under braking, but the stewards decided no further investigation was needed. item.title: Golf’s 2026 Turkey Awards Show The Sport’s Ugly Side
item.description: John (Jack) Power-Imagn Images The 2026 season for professional golf was a mess of bad behavior and real-life scares. While fans watched great shots, the year also delivered a list of moments that made the sport look bad. Yahoo Sports compiled the annual Turkey Awards to honor these dubious achievements. Bad Behavior On The Course Some of the worst moments came from players losing their tempers in plain sight. Sergio Garcia slammed his club into a water cooler at the 2026 Masters after a bad drive. The outburst earned him a code-of-conduct warning just two holes later. Then there was the incident at the Waste Management Open involving YouTube streamer Jack Doherty. The drama wasn’t limited to the course. Garrett Clark, a cofounder of Good Good Golf, pushed creator Alexis Miestowski to the ground during a Callaway driver promo video. The company claimed it was a spoof of a horror movie, but viewers were simply horrified. The fallout was swift and sweeping. Dick’s and Golf Galaxy took the merchandise down, Callaway cut its connection, and the company’s CEO and president were dismissed. Good Good also pulled out as the title sponsor for its own PGA Tour event. Off-Course Chaos And Health Scars Financial mismanagement and health scares defined the darker side of the tour this year. The breakaway LIV league filed for Chapter 11 after leaving more than 1,000 vendors unpaid. Despite this, the league dished out more than $15 million to its executives before folding. On a more personal note, veteran caddie Henry Diana faced a life-or-death situation during the AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am in February. His kidney function had dropped so low that working could cost him his life. On Friday night, he contacted his player Harry Hall with a frightening message, according to reports. “H, I’m at the hospital. If I caddie tomorrow, I could die,” he told Hall. Diana eventually stepped away from the Tour to undergo a kidney transplant. His story highlights the hidden dangers lurking on tour that fans rarely see.

item.description: Titans' Cam Ward is one loss away from making bleak NFL history originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tennessee Titans are not having a good 2026 NFL season. Cam Ward has shown some promise this year, which has been encouraging, but their defense is horrible, and the team has a 1-9 record. With how poorly the Titans have played, it shouldn't be a surprise that Ward has made some NFL history no player wants to set. But heading into Week 12 against the Jacksonville Jaguars , Ward is on the cusp of some all-time horrible history. As ESPN Research highlighted , if Ward loses to the Jaguars in Week 12, then he will have broken the record for most losses by a quarterback in their first two NFL seasons since at least 1950. Cam Ward is one loss away from breaking NFL QB losing record "Titans QB Cam Ward is 4-23 as a starting QB," ESPN Research shared. "A 24th loss would break a tie for the most losses by a starting QB in his first two NFL seasons since 1950." Ward has only three wins in his NFL career, with his 23 losses over the past two years being an incomprehensible stretch of losing for the second-year QB out of Miami. At 1-9 this year, with their lone win coming against the Indianapolis Colts back in Week 6, Ward has quite the history of losing in his career. Through two years and 26 games played, he has 23 losses. One more loss, and he'll have the most losses by any quarterback ever through the first two NFL seasons. With the Jaguars, the current AFC South division leaders, on the schedule for Week 12, it wouldn't be a surprise for the Titans to lose this week and give Ward the record. But even if they beat the Jaguars, Ward is still likely to break this record if he's healthy. After facing Jacksonville in Week 12, the Titans have the following opponents on their schedule: Washington Commanders , Detroit Lions , Colts, Las Vegas Raiders , Pittsburgh Steelers , and Houston Texans . While the Titans could potentially beat the Colts, Raiders, Steelers, and Texans, the Commanders are playing well lately, and the Lions are one of the best teams in the league. Seeing this Titans team win out this year would be maybe the biggest surprise the NFL has seen in a long time. Ward hasn't broken this record, but it is very likely he'll break it at some point this year. item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram.
